title: Decide on unaided work
statement: Base decisions on the first unaided check and let a high-stakes score count only unaided work, because doing something with cues is not doing it unaided.
example: Support is labelled 0 to 3, from none to worked steps or feedback, and fades to 0 by the check.
detail: The assessment pattern library in the reading project's knowledge base labels every task with its support, from 0 for none to 3 for worked steps or feedback, and with the inference it allows, unaided or with standard or guided supports, and fades support across a lesson from warm-up through practice to the check and transfer (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0158-assessment-pattern-library-brainlift.qmd`). Supported steps serve mainly for feedback and move an estimate only a little; high-stakes decisions rest on the first unaided check or transfer task, and a claim says whether it holds with standard cues or unaided. The assessment pack guide adds, for AP-style constructed responses, that scaffolding changes a task's difficulty and so how attainment is read (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0153-assessment-pack-brainlift.qmd`). Each task's support is labelled, and every result is stated with the support it was earned under.

evidence.quote: base high-stakes decisions on the first unaided check (or transfer task) that follows.
State the claim to match support.
S: 0 = none; 1 = cues/examples; 2 = guided prompts; 3 = worked steps/feedback.
structure each lesson as a fade from high-support learning to low-support evidence.
The amount of scaffolding and guidance in a task directly affects its difficulty and therefore has implications for how we interpret student attainment.
"can do X with cues" ≠ "unaided"
The mastery claim states its support level ("unaided" vs "with cues"); high-stakes scores only the unaided check
It must be unmistakably the student thinking alone: exploring, writing, evaluating
On a blank answer, it offered: “An ensign carries a flag. What is Iago’s flag hiding?” That’s a restrained but interpretation-shaping hint.
If the student requests instructional help, we record the attempt as assisted and later offer a fresh independent opportunity.
A high-school mathematics experiment found that unrestricted GPT assistance improved practice performance while reducing subsequent unaided performance.
This is a warning to test independent learning, not proof of the same effect in English.
During practice, grades rose 48% with GPT Base and 127% with GPT Tutor.
On the unassisted exam, the GPT Base group scored 17% *worse* than controls.
It erased most of the harm, but it did **not** beat the control group on the exam.
A reveal is supported review, not unaided recall.
Assistance and model reveals are honestly labelled; no live AI diagnosis is implied.
Scaffolded in-session success is not delayed unaided mastery.
A question counts as right only if no wrong answer was ever recorded against
supported retry counted as first independent success
